::: {#exm-rarity-die}
#### Rarity of the outcomes of a die

<!-- no-figure: the example is two numbers -->

Let $X$ be the roll of a fair six-sided die.
Each [outcome](https://morrison-lab.github.io/pds/probability-basics.html#def-experiment-outcome)
has [probability](https://morrison-lab.github.io/pds/probability-basics.html#def-probability) $1/6$.
So each has [rarity](#def-rarity) $\rarityf{x} = 6$:
one roll in six.

Suppose the die is loaded so that a six has probability $1/2$.
Then $\rarityf{6} = 2$.
If the other five faces share the rest equally,
each has $\rarityf{x} = 10$.
The more probable an outcome, the lower its rarity.

:::
